svg.title: Flower Anatomy Drag & Drop Learning Interface
svg.desc: Educational interactive tool for learning flower anatomy with 10 labeled parts.

text.tspan: Match each numbered label on the flower
diagram with the correct anatomical term

g.text: Match part names from the Word Bank
Over 80% of flowering plants depend on animal pollinators
like bees, butterflies, and hummingbirds for reproduction!
Use these clues to match each number to a part:
Colorful, leaf-like structures that attract pollinators
Green, leaf-like structures that protect the flower bud before it opens
The male reproductive organ, consisting of anther + filament
The female reproductive organ, consisting of stigma + style + ovary
The tip of the stamen that produces and holds pollen grains
The thin stalk that supports the anther
The swollen base of the pistil that contains ovules (future seeds)
The long tube connecting the stigma to the ovary
The sticky tip at the top of the pistil that catches pollen
The thickened part of the stem where flower parts are attached
Remember — Stamen = Anther + Filament (male parts), and Pistil = Stigma + Style + Ovary (female parts).
Attract pollinators with color and scent
Protect the flower bud before it blooms
Supports the anther on a slender stalk
Contains ovules that develop into seeds after fertilization
Connects the stigma to the ovary; pollen tube grows through it
Sticky surface that receives pollen during pollination
Thickened area of the stem that holds all flower parts
How many did you get right? Give yourself a score out of 10! 🌸
Use the numbered labels (①–⑩) on the diagram to check your answers.
This will clear your progress and reset
the activity to its initial state.
Close this popup by clicking ✕ or the backdrop
Review the diagram and Word Bank again
💪 Practice makes perfect — try again and ace it!
